articles.abstractText:
Background

Climate-related disasters increasingly affect community health, health care access, and disaster preparedness, particularly in disaster-prone Gulf Coast communities. Although climate dashboards have expanded access to environmental data, many function primarily as static repositories with limited integration of health data or operational decision support capabilities.

Objective

This study aimed to identify stakeholder-informed design priorities and implementation considerations for a climate and health dashboard to support disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and community decision-making.

Methods

We conducted semistructured interviews with 7 multisector stakeholders representing academic research, community-based organizations, public health, emergency preparedness, and disaster recovery settings in Houston, Texas. Interviews explored current use of climate and health data, desired dashboard features, usability considerations, data integration needs, and sustainability priorities. Transcripts were analyzed using the Rapid and Rigorous Qualitative Data Analysis (RADaR) technique.

Results

Participants described a need for dashboards that could support decision-making rather than simply display data. Priorities included the integration of climate, health, infrastructure, and social vulnerability data; interactive mapping and layered visualizations; local geographic detail; AI-assisted interpretation and plain language summaries; and tools useful to both community and research audiences. Potential uses included emergency preparedness, targeted outreach during disasters, resource allocation, policy advocacy, and community education.

Conclusions

Findings suggest that effective climate and health dashboards require not only technical functionality but also community-centered design, operational usability, and sustainable implementation infrastructure. These findings are preliminary and may inform future studies aimed at developing dashboards designed to support community-focused disaster preparedness and response.

articles.abstractText:
Introduction

Delirium occurs in 20%-40% of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) patients and is associated with increased morbidity, mortality, healthcare expenditure, and long-term psychological consequences. Despite the implementation of delirium screening in the Children's Hospital Colorado PICU in 2019 using the Cornell Assessment of Pediatric Delirium (CAPD) screening tool, screening compliance remained <50%. This project aimed to improve delirium screening compliance in the Children's Hospital Colorado PICU from 48% of scoring opportunities to 80% over 13 months.

Methods

This quality improvement initiative was conducted in a 48-bed quaternary PICU and included 4,195 patients admitted from April 2024 to April 2025. We developed key driver diagrams and process maps using nursing surveys and workflow insights. Interventions included electronic health record embedded CAPD reminders, multidisciplinary delirium and CAPD tool education, and dissemination of a departmental delirium clinical practice resource. We extracted data from an internally developed and validated electronic health record delirium dashboard. We used statistical process control charts to evaluate outcomes.

Results

CAPD scoring compliance increased from a baseline of 48.0% to 75.9% following interventions. Positive delirium screening rates decreased from 54.6% to 44.3%. Postintervention nursing surveys showed that 100% of respondents reported a neutral or positive impact on workflow, and the proportion citing lack of reminders as a barrier decreased from 41% to less than 10%.

Conclusions

A multidisciplinary, workflow-integrated approach substantially improved CAPD screening compliance in a high-volume, high-acuity PICU. Electronic health record-embedded reminders and targeted education are low-cost strategies for improving delirium screening adherence without increasing perceived nursing workload.

articles.abstractText:
Context

Medical Aid in Dying (MAiD) refers to the practice of a physician prescribing aid-in-dying medications to a terminally ill patient at their request that must be self-administered to end their life. MAiD is legal in several states for individuals who meet specific requirements.

Objectives

We describe the development and implementation of a MAiD program at a comprehensive cancer center as part of the hospitals' comprehensive end-of-life options.

Methods

Upon passing of MAiD legislation in New York in 2026, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center convened a multidisciplinary group to guide planning and implementation across clinical, operational, ethical, educational and staff support domains in accordance with state law and institutional values. An institutional policy is developed to support operations. A dedicated team will be responsible for handling initial inquiries to medication prescribing. Surveys assessed clinical team sentiment and willingness to participate. Role-based education will include serious illness communication training, and a communications plan will ensure hospital wide awareness. A prospective quality dashboard will capture quality and process measures. Data will be collected to meet state-required reporting and to guide development of best practices RESULTS: Implementation will be completed within approximately 6 months of the law being signed. Data collection will be ongoing; the dashboard will enable monthly monitoring of referral volume by location, demographics, and timeliness. Planned analysis and weekly huddles will assess equity of access, program capacity, targets for process improvement, provision of high-quality palliative care support for all patients, clinicians, patient, and family feedback.

Conclusion

A structured, multidisciplinary approach enabled rapid operationalization of MAiD at a cancer center while prioritizing patient-centered care, legal compliance, ethical standards, considerations for oncologists and staff preparedness. Ongoing measurement will inform program refinement to promote equitable access and high-quality care.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 9 encompasses Kentucky and Tennessee; Appalachian regions with a rurality rate exceeding 50% and some of the nation's highest cancer incidence. Veterans face significant geographical barriers to receiving specialty infusion care, requiring them to choose between long-distance travel to main VA campuses or fragmented care through community partners.

Objectives

Describe the implementation of two Close to Me (CTM) remote infusion sites while evaluating outcomes, including patient safety and pharmaceutical scope of care. To quantify the economic impact while describing practice innovations and implications for the program's scalability.

Practice description

Lexington VA Health Care System and Tennessee Valley Healthcare System launched remote infusion sites in two rural locations. Compounded sterile preparations were prepared at their main campuses and transported to remote sites, where interprofessional care teams provided treatments.

Practice innovation

The CTM program adapted home infusion principles to a structured hub-and spoke model, making use of existing USP <797> and <800> compliant compounding suites. Innovations included maximizing alternative formulations, adjusting medication protocols, and expansion into additional subspecialties to improve Veteran access.

Evaluation methods

Data were extracted from a custom analytics dashboard and Veteran Signal satisfaction surveys collected from June 2025 to June 2026.

Results

One hundred eighty-three Veterans have been served through the CTM program to include 166 unique patients seen face to face by CTM providers with 61 Veterans receiving infusions, saving over 100,000 travel miles from all appointment types. Zero infusion reactions were recorded, medication waste was minimal, and Veteran satisfaction and trust in the program was high. Medication cost avoidance totaled approximately $660,000.

Conclusion

The VISN 9 CTM program demonstrates that high-quality, safe, and cost-effective specialty infusion care can be delivered remotely to Veterans in Appalachia, offering a scalable model for expanding access into other rural regions.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Digital platforms that integrate continuous glucose monitoring, patient-generated data, and clinical decision support could enable more proactive pediatric type 1 diabetes (T1D) care. Sustained uptake of digital platforms in routine practice is limited, and the evidence of effectiveness is mixed. Implementation science approaches are needed to clarify how context, workflows, and strategies shape adoption and outcomes. Haibu Diabetes is a new platform that brings together wearable, patient-reported, and clinical diabetes data to generate personalized, data-driven insights for patients and clinicians.

Objective

This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and implementation processes of Haibu Diabetes in routine pediatric T1D care using a hybrid design guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model.

Methods

We will conduct a nonrandomized, quasi-experimental, type 2 hybrid implementation-effectiveness trial at a hospital that provides multidisciplinary pediatric diabetes care. Youth aged 3 to less than 18 years with T1D and caregivers will be onboarded to Haibu Diabetes as part of routine workflows; health care providers will use a clinician dashboard to review data, assign tasks/forms, and communicate asynchronously. Effectiveness analyses will compare Haibu Diabetes users to a matched control group drawn from the BC Pediatric Diabetes Registry. Effectiveness outcomes are hemoglobin A1c, continuous glucose monitoring device-derived time in range over 12 months, and diabetes self-care behaviors. Implementation outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model that links determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes. These outcomes will include reach, adoption, feasibility, acceptability, and maintenance. Health care improvement outcomes will include patient and caregiver experience, clinician experience, and operational workflow indicators.

Results

Study funding commenced in January 2023. Patient recruitment began in September 2026, and 7 participants had consented as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by December 2027, with analysis to follow. Study findings are expected to be published in summer 2028.

Conclusions

This trial will generate real-world evidence on both effectiveness and the conditions required to implement and sustain a data-integrating digital platform in pediatric T1D care, informing scale-up and optimization.

articles.abstractText:
Background and objectives

Lean production techniques have been widely adopted in manufacturing to reduce waste, optimize processes, and improve efficiency. With the rising focus on sustainability across economic, environmental, and social dimensions, attention has turned to healthcare settings. However, the application of Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM) in hospitals remains relatively unexplored.

Methods

This study addresses that gap by implementing a Sus-VSM approach in the preoperative and postoperative phases of 3 surgery types: general surgery, urology, and obstetrics at a major hospital. We collected 6 months of operational data, identifying key inefficiencies. A current-state VSM was created, followed by Lean-based interventions including 5S, visualization, and forecasting.

Results

Results revealed an 11.5% reduction in anesthesia paperwork time and improved bed-management planning. Additionally, we evaluated the hospital's economic, social, and environmental performance using adapted metrics. Findings indicate particularly high social sustainability (97.85%), moderate environmental performance (77.6%), and an 80.2% economic rating.

Conclusion

By integrating triple-bottom-line principles with Lean thinking, this study presents a structured methodology for advancing both operational efficiency and institutional sustainability in healthcare. These findings support the broader adoption of Sus-VSM and point to the need for life-cycle assessments and longitudinal research to validate long-term impacts on healthcare delivery.

articles.title: In Situ vs. Monitor-Based: Evaluating Augmented Reality for Ultrasound-Guided Peripheral Venous Catheter Insertion.
articles.authorString: Souadda ZM, Olivares A, Zine Y, Drouin S.

journal.title: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics

articles.abstractText: Ultrasound-guided placement of peripheral venous catheters (PVCs) is a cognitively demanding routine medical procedure that requires operators to constantly divide their attention between the ultrasound display and the spatial relationship among the probe, the needle, and the vein. As a result of this difficulty, the procedure is associated with a high complication rate for patients. The goal of this paper is to evaluate the potential of augmented reality (AR) to facilitate the procedure for clinicians by displaying ultrasound (US) images in situ. To do so, we conducted a mixed-design user study involving 30 healthcare professionals (9 experts and 21 novices). The study was conducted within a virtual reality (VR) environment to provide a standardized and controlled setting. We compared two visualization modes: a conventional monitor-based setup replicating the standard clinical display, and an AR-assisted interface where the ultrasound image is spatially anchored directly under the probe and augmented with real-time distance cues. Participants performed ten insertions per condition. We measured procedure time, successful insertion attempts, tissue perforations, and needle-beam alignment accuracy, while also assessing perceived workload (NASA-TLX) and system usability (SUS). Experts completed the procedure in 524.2±154 s with AR, compared to 1125.7±472 s using the traditional monitor-based layout, whereas novices completed the procedure in 746±410 s, compared to 1165±597 s. Spatial accuracy in novices increased from 50.6±8.2% to 65.9±13.6%, corresponding to a reduction in mean targeting error from 1.26 mm to 0.79 mm. The AR condition also greatly reduced tissue perforations in novices, decreasing from 29.4±45.6 to 3.0±2.7. Participants reported a lower perceived workload with AR, which indicates that placing the ultrasound image directly under the probe helps reduce attention shifts and supports spatial understanding. These findings demonstrate that AR-based in situ visualization can meaningfully enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and safety of ultrasound-guided procedures.

articles.abstractText: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics yield large-scale, high-dimensional datasets. However, cross-feature integrative exploration is constrained, since most current platforms support a single data type and lack interactive visualization for multi-feature analysis. To address this unmet need, we developed Cell3D, an accessible and versatile interactive platform designed to advance integrative multi-level feature analysis. Cell3D curates 898 publicly available datasets, comprising 397 single-cell and 501 spatial transcriptomic datasets, encompassing 2 924 646 single cells and spatial spots across 105 diseases, 756 cell types, and 83 organs/tissues from 11 species. The database integrates twelve mainstream functional annotation systems, providing a comprehensive landscape for dissecting molecular features across spatial and cellular dimensions. Users can explore data at multiple levels, from gene expression and cell clusters to pathway activities and clinical phenotypes. Cell3D offers a suite of user-friendly functionalities, including customizable 2D/3D interactive visualization for dynamic multi-level feature projection, flexible data integration with automatic recognition, quantitative crosstalk analysis, and microenvironment-focused integrative analysis supporting disease research and biomarker discovery. Collectively, Cell3D enables exploration of tissue microenvironments at both cellular and spatial resolutions, bridging molecular perturbations and tissue architecture in health and disease. The database is freely accessible at https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/Cell3D.

articles.abstractText: Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) is a serious complication of abdominal and pelvic radiotherapy. Its mechanism is complex, and traditional treatment methods are difficult to achieve precise intervention and efficacy visualization. Bardoxolone methyl (CDDO-Me) has a therapeutic effect on intestinal injury as an Nrf2 activator. However, there are limitations such as uncontrolled drug release and lack of efficacy visualization. To address this problem, we prepared a sodium alginate/hyaluronic acid (AL/HA) pH-responsive oral hydrogel loaded with CDDO-Me, and introduced melanin nanoparticles (SMNP) with enhanced MRI signal to achieve non-invasive visualization of the distribution, localization and retention of the hydrogel in rats. The hydrogel exhibited resistance to gastric acid, mucoadhesive properties, and prolonged retention in the small intestine and colon, thus achieving controlled intestinal release of drugs. In addition, our research suggested that the oral CDDO-Me@AL/HA@SMNP hydrogel could alleviate intestinal oxidative stress injury and down-regulate pro-inflammatory cytokines in mouse models. These effects may be associated with Nrf2 activation and ROS clearance, and may also involve the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway. Overall, our research indicated that the CDDO-Me@AL/HA@SMNP hydrogel integrates therapeutic efficacy with MRI-based visualization/tracking capabilities for RIII. These findings represent a preclinical proof-of-concept, and further optimization, safety evaluation, and translational studies are required before any potential clinical application.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Fluorescence-guided (FG) surgery using near-infrared imaging has been adopted to enhance intraoperative visualization in multiple surgical fields. In foregut surgery, calibration tubes are routinely used to calibrate crural closure but due to limited visibility carry a risk of iatrogenic injury, including esophageal or gastric perforation. Techniques that improve visualization of these devices may support safer intraoperative management.

Case presentation

A 75-year-old woman with a symptomatic paraesophageal hiatal hernia and partial gastric volvulus underwent robotic paraesophageal hiatal hernia repair with Toupet fundoplication. A FG gastric calibration tube (size 40 Fr, Endolumik Inc.), was inserted under near-infrared visualization and advanced down the esophagus and into the stomach. The device was used to (1) evacuate gastric contents, (2) guide tube positioning past the gastroesophageal junction, (3) inform mediastinal dissection/esophageal mobilization, (4) enable FG measuring of the length of esophageal mobilization below the diaphragm, and (5) calibrate both crural closure and fundoplication. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 1 and reported resolution of dysphagia at 8-week follow-up.

Discussion

This case demonstrates the feasibility of FG calibration during robotic paraesophageal hernia repair. Continuous visualization of the calibration device provided an additional intraoperative reference during dissection in the setting of distorted anatomy. This approach may offer improved orientation compared with conventional calibration techniques, although its effect on clinical outcomes remains unknown.

Objectives

This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). The objectives are as follows: The objectives of this living evidence map are to: systematically map the breadth, scope, and characteristics of the global literature on the relationship of climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents, and fossil fuels with human health and well-being; enable ongoing, up-to-date access to the evolving evidence base through a living approach (encompassing content currency and adjustment of methods); enable identification of clusters of well-researched areas and evidence gaps; enable flexible, accelerated identification, visualization, selection, analysis, and export of records according to the needs of a diverse group of interest holders via an interactive interface and filtering via a dedicated taxonomy; enable the continuous monitoring of a specific topic of interest; and evaluate the rigor, legitimacy, and utility of an AI-supported living evidence mapping approach. articles.abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate the clinical efficacy of full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression technique performed under local anesthesia for Far-out syndrome (FOS) and to describe its technical nuances.

Methods

Between March 2023 and March 2025, 27 consecutive FOS patients underwent full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression via a single-portal paravertebral approach under local anesthesia. This approach allows medial extension of decompression into the intraforaminal zone when necessary to achieve adequate release of the L5 exiting nerve root. Clinical outcomes were assessed using VAS, ODI, and modified MacNab criteria preoperatively and at 3 days, 1, 3, and 12 months postoperatively. Key procedural steps were detailed, and outcomes compared with literature.

Results

Mean age was 69 ± 12 years; mean operative time 102 ± 28 min.

Pathology

33% pure bony stenosis, 67% combined with disc herniation. VAS improved from 7.5 ± 0.9 preoperatively to 1.5 ± 1.1 at 12 months (P < 0.0001). ODI decreased from 71 ± 5% to 16 ± 7% (P < 0.0001). MacNab criteria: 89% excellent/good, 7.4% fair, 3.7% poor. Suboptimal outcomes: one preoperative level misidentification, one residual radicular symptom, and one epineurial tear (no deficit). Comparative analysis confirmed favorable outcomes versus other techniques.

Conclusion

Full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression under local anesthesia is effective and safe for FOS, offering real-time patient feedback, avoidance of general anesthesia, and minimal tissue trauma, making it suitable for the often-elderly FOS population.

articles.abstractText: Transcervical submandibular sialadenectomy remains the standard approach for submandibular gland excision but carries the risk of marginal mandibular nerve injury and cervical scarring. Endoscopic-assisted transoral submandibular sialadenectomy has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative that may improve visualization and reduce morbidity. To evaluate the feasibility and safety of endoscopic-assisted transoral submandibular sialadenectomy and assess postoperative functional and quality-of-life outcomes in a single-arm cohort of patients with chronic submandibular sialadenitis. This prospective study included 20 adult patients with chronic submandibular sialadenitis who underwent endoscopic-assisted transoral submandibular sialadenectomy between January 2020 and December 2022. Intraoperative and postoperative complications were recorded. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10), Speech Handicap Index (SHI), visual analogue scale (VAS) for pain, and clinical evaluation of taste disturbance, tongue paresthesia, and tongue deviation. Oral health-related quality of life was assessed using the modified Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14) questionnaire. All procedures were completed successfully without conversion to a transcervical approach. No major intraoperative complications or permanent neurovascular injuries occurred. Minor wound dehiscence developed in two patients and oral candidiasis in one patient, all of which resolved with conservative treatment. Transient postoperative taste abnormalities, tongue paresthesia, tongue deviation, dysphagia, and speech impairment were observed but resolved completely during follow-up. Oral health-related quality of life improved significantly, with all patients demonstrating minimal-impact OHIP-14 scores at 3 months postoperatively (p = 0.002; effect size r = 0.89). In this prospective single-arm feasibility study, endoscopic-assisted transoral submandibular sialadenectomy was successfully performed in all patients and was associated with low morbidity, favorable functional recovery, and improved oral health-related quality of life.

articles.abstractText:
Introduction

Ergonomic injuries are a common and preventable type of workplace injury that may result in persistent pain and opioid use or misuse, and previous studies have linked occupational injuries to subsequent opioid misuse. Despite a decrease in opioid prescriptions, opioid-related overdose deaths in New York State (NYS) continue to increase, requiring further exploration of contributing factors. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between ergonomic workplace injury rates and opioid-related outcomes in NYS.  METHODS: County-level rates of NYS Workers' Compensation Claims (WCC) from 2015-2021 were analyzed, focusing on sprain, strain, and tear injuries. These injury claim rates were compared with county-level opioid-related data from the NYS Opioid Data Dashboard. A linear mixed-effects model, with year fixed effects and county-level clustering, was used to estimate the association between opioid prescription rates, WCC rates, and opioid-related mortality rates. The association between prescribing and mortality outcomes was modified by WCC rates was also examined.

Results

There was a greater overlap between high WCC rates and high opioid indicator rates observed in non-metro counties over metro counties. Health Care and Social Assistance, Public Administration, Retail Trade, and Educational Services were the most represented industries in ergonomic WCCs across the state. There was evidence of effect modification by WCC injury rates on the association between opioid prescription and overdose mortality rates, for opioids (B=-3.03, 95% CI: -4.58, -1.48) and opioid pain relievers (B=-3.75, 95% CI: -5.34, -2.17), showing that the association between opioid prescribing and mortality rates weakened among counties with higher WCC injury rates.

Conclusions

Despite progress in reducing opioid prescription rates in NYS, workplace ergonomic injuries resulting in strains, sprains, and tears may be contributing to overdose deaths, including from opioids. Workplace ergonomic safety campaigns may be an avenue for prevention of opioid-related overdoses in NYS.

articles.abstractText: Preoperative planning in orthopaedic trauma remains largely experience-driven despite advances in imaging and predictive modeling. Although three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions improve fracture visualization, they do not routinely predict biomechanical stability across competing fixation strategies. Automated segmentation and finite element analysis (FEA) offer the potential to transition trauma planning from primarily anatomic to a method by which constructs may be optimized. This narrative review summarizes the current state of 3D planning and segmentation, describes the principles and established applications of FEA, delineates the workflow of finite element modeling in clinical practice, and integrates representative clinical cases to illustrate how plate positioning and screw configuration affect construct stability and works alongside the surgeon to help inform decisions. Broader implications for hospital systems, patients, and industry are discussed, along with future integration into navigation, robotics, and intraoperative 3D imaging workflows.

articles.abstractText: Stress is a major contributor to physical and mental health disorders, underscoring the need for reliable and interpretable detection systems. We present an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates electrocardiogram (ECG), electrodermal activity (EDA), and respiration signals using modality-specific neural architectures complemented by feature-based classical models. To ensure robustness and generalizability, the framework was evaluated under both subject-independent and subject-dependent protocols. Results show that multimodal fusion consistently outperformed single modalities, achieving 94.8% accuracy, 93.9% F1-score, and 0.97 AUC under subject-independent validation, compared with 86-91% accuracy for individual signals. In subject-dependent experiments, performance reached 97.2% accuracy and 96.8% F1-score. Comparative analysis with recent state-of-the-art methods demonstrated the competitiveness of our approach, while ablation studies confirmed the contribution of each modality and fusion strategy. Statistical significance testing with (p < 0.05) further validated the reliability of these gains. Importantly, interpretability analyses using Grad-CAM and attention visualization provided physiological insights, revealing that the model emphasizes clinically meaningful regions such as ECG R-peaks and phasic EDA fluctuations. By uniting high performance, robustness, and interpretability, this work advances stress detection research and offers a physiologically grounded framework for continuous mental health monitoring.

articles.abstractText: BackgroundBreast cancer remains a major global health concern, and early and accurate detection is critical for improving clinical outcomes. However, variations in lesion characteristics and imaging conditions in Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) images present substantial challenges for automated breast tumor classification.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a robust and interpretable deep learning framework, termed RA-BCNet-PReLU, by integrating residual attention mechanisms with Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) activation for accurate multi-class breast tumor classification.MethodsThe proposed framework employs a structured processing pipeline comprising Min-Max normalization, stratified sampling, and targeted image augmentation for data preprocessing and generalization. Lesion segmentation is performed using a convolutional neural network (CNN), with segmentation further optimized using the Dynamic Hybrid Grey Wolf-Sunflower Optimization (DHGWSFO) algorithm. Subsequently, handcrafted shape, color, and spatial descriptors are integrated with deep features extracted using ResNet-50 to obtain a comprehensive lesion representation. The fused features are then classified using a residual attention-based CNN with PReLU activation. The model was evaluated on a DBT mammography dataset and externally validated on the CBIS-DDSM dataset. Model reliability was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, ANOVA, paired t-tests, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, while Grad-CAM was employed to improve model interpretability.ResultsThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.87% ± 0.42 on the DBT dataset and 98.72% ± 0.35 on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, with corresponding AUC values of 0.967 and 0.981, respectively. Statistical analyses demonstrated the reliability of the obtained results, while Grad-CAM visualizations highlighted clinically relevant regions contributing to the model's predictions.ConclusionThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU framework demonstrates high classification performance, robustness, and interpretability across DBT and external mammography datasets. Its integration of optimized lesion segmentation, hybrid feature representation, residual attention, and explainable visualization indicates its potential as an effective computer-aided tool for automated breast cancer detection and clinical decision support.

articles.abstractText: Danshen injection is used as an adjunctive cardiovascular therapy in some Chinese hospitals, but retrospective evaluations are vulnerable to exposure misclassification, nonuniform measurement timing, baseline imbalance, complete-case selection, and time-related bias. This article presents an audit-ready electronic health record workflow for adults with acute myocardial infarction who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and received inpatient aspirin plus clopidogrel. The workflow adds TCM-specific fields for syndrome differentiation, indication, prescriber specialty, product formulation, and administration timing; separates outcome-specific analysis sets; and defines propensity-score overlap weighting for the population with clinical equipoise. An archived 89-patient cohort (45 with documented Danshen administration and 44 controls) illustrates the analytical sequence. In the archived file, only analysis-file checks, model fitting, balance diagnostics, bootstrap estimation, and visualization could be executed. Source-record steps requiring unrecovered treatment timestamps, echocardiographic metadata, assay boundaries, exact exclusion variables, or adjudicated events are presented as workflow specifications and were not treated as completed procedures. The groups were strongly imbalanced at baseline. In the primary ANCOVA using HC3 standard errors, the adjusted between-group difference in pre-discharge left ventricular ejection fraction was 6.82 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 4.54-9.10). The separate overlap-weighted estimate was 6.95 percentage points (patient-level bootstrap standard error: 1.08; 95% percentile confidence interval: 4.90-9.07; 2,000 resamples). These estimates are numerical demonstrations rather than causal treatment effects. Database-coded cardiovascular and bleeding indicators were excluded because component events, dates, follow-up completeness, and a common time origin could not be verified. The workflow has not been externally validated and should be considered a pilot demonstration.

articles.abstractText:
Objective

The Ambulatory Care Model Redesign (ACMR) initiative sought to improve patient-centered, team-based oncology care in a leading US cancer specialty hospital by strengthening care coordination, optimizing care team roles, improving scheduling reliability, and increasing operational efficiency across ambulatory clinics. The initiative sought to address increasing care complexity, workforce strain, and patient throughput challenges by redesigning care delivery through interprofessional collaboration and agile implementation strategies.

Methods

ACMR was implemented as a quality improvement initiative using Plan-Do-Check-Act methodology, agile project management, and a tri-level governance structure involving executive leaders, operational leaders, and frontline care teams. Key interventions included pooled rooming; top-of-license role optimization for medical assistants, registered nurses, and advanced practice providers; embedded disease-team scheduling; standardized point-of-service scheduling workflows; expanded electronic health record (EHR) checkout functionality; and real-time performance dashboards. Outcomes were monitored using key performance indicators, including order entry, same-day scheduling, EHR in-basket turnaround, checkout completion, and patient experience.

Findings

ACMR produced measurable improvements in clinic operations, care coordination, and patient experience. Orders placed before checkout increased by 15.4 percentage points (pp), same-day checkout completion rose by 30.0 pp, and appointment scheduling before patient departure improved by nearly 20.0 pp. EHR in-basket optimization reduced scheduling-related messages per provider by 44.0%, with 80.0% addressed within 48 hours. Patient satisfaction improved by 15.3 pp for ease of scheduling and by 11.3 pp for perceived care coordination. Embedding schedulers within disease-specific teams also improved interprofessional collaboration and role clarity. Despite these gains, barriers including physician hesitancy, staffing variability, and dashboard fatigue highlighted the need for sustained leadership engagement, cultural alignment, and adaptive change management.

Conclusion

Structured ambulatory oncology redesign supported by interprofessional governance, role optimization, EHR-enabled workflows, and real-time data can improve access, coordination, and patient experience. Sustaining gains requires continued leadership engagement, staffing alignment, and iterative performance monitoring.

articles.abstractText: High-quality care transitions are essential for sepsis survivors at risk of readmission and long-term complications. These complex innovations require coordination across organizations, individuals, and processes. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) offers a systematic approach to identifying multi-level implementation determinants, but translating them into actionable strategies remains challenging. This study examines the representation of implementation determinants across CFIR domains and visualizes their cross-domain interconnectedness. CFIR-guided, semi-structured pre-implementation needs assessment interviews were conducted with stakeholders involved in sepsis care transitions across five hospital-home healthcare (HHC) dyads. Thirty-two themes identified through deductive-inductive coding were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs and visualized using node diagrams. Sixty-one interviews with 91 stakeholders identified 32 themes spanning all five CFIR domains, with most themes mapping to multiple domains. Access to Care theme mapped across all five domains, while External Policies and Incentives and Informal Caregiving themes were represented only once. Implementation Process domain was most represented and Innovation least represented. All constructs within the Implementation Process and Individual Characteristics domains were captured. Node diagrams illustrated the depth and interconnected influence of determinants in sepsis care transitions. Stakeholders identified complexity emerged across technical, structural, and policy domains as both an innovation feature and contextual determinants of sepsis care transitions. CFIR mapping and visualization provided a structured approach to characterizing pre-implementation complexity in sepsis care transitions. Examining determinant representation and cross-domain interconnectedness may help identify cross-cutting, potentially high-leverage implementation needs and inform strategy selection and tailoring for complex hospital-to-home interventions.

articles.abstractText: Plasma nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomics offers a scalable molecular readout linking genetic variation, environmental exposure, and clinical physiology to future disease risk. Existing resources typically address metabolite-disease associations, metabolite quantitative trait loci, or prediction separately, with limited support for integrated mediation and longitudinal risk stratification. MetabHub (https://www.metabhub.net) is a web-based resource built from individual-level UK Biobank data, comprising 364 795 European participants, 251 plasma NMR traits, 129 clinical measurements, 54 environmental exposures, genome-wide variants, and 57 incident diseases. It maps sex-combined and sex-specific associations across measurements, exposures, genotypes, metabolites, and diseases, yielding 2 950 764 significant associations. Using two-step screening and natural effect models, MetabHub identifies 1 886 224 significant clinical measurement, environmental factor, and genotype mediation pathways. It also provides metabolite-based prediction models for incident disease using penalized logistic regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron, together with an online interface for applying pre-trained models to user-uploaded profiles. Model-derived metabolomic risk scores are further evaluated using Cox regression and survival stratification over ~14 years of follow-up. Global search, interactive visualization, downloadable tables, prediction, and stratification modules support mechanistic discovery and metabolomics-informed precision prevention.

articles.abstractText:
Objectives

Early diagnosis of Biliary atresia (BA) improves native liver and overall survival. Pale stools are a characteristic symptom and might be detected by deep learning image recognition. We tested convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify pictures of pale and healthy stools and compare the results with stool color card (SCC) assessment of health care professionals (HCP) and non-health care professionals (NHCP).

Methods

One thousand six hundred and sixteen stool photos with diagnostic labels including BA and healthy controls were graded as pale or normal according to the SCC. A subset of photos (33 BA and 241 healthy) was presented to HCP and NHCP for SCC assessment to evaluate accuracy and interobserver reliability. For CNN model selection and training all images were split into training, validation, and test sets. Different visualization strategies and secondary data augmentation were used for explainability and estimating robustness.

Results

In SCC assessment, sensitivity by NHCP trended lower than HCP (86.4% vs. 97.3%), while there were no differences in specificity. Intra-cohort agreement on classification of BA stools (pale vs. normal) was also lower for NHCP than for HCP (36.4% vs. 78.8%), while no significant difference was observed in healthy stools. The selected CNN (ResNet18) correctly classified 97.5% of pale and 98.5% of normal labeled stools, also showing robust results in explainability methods.

Conclusions

The high accuracy of CNN shows the potential for a digital stool color screening. In contrast, NHCP assessment of pale stools tends to be inconsistent, and there is high interobserver variability among HCP and NHCP.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Obesity frequently co-occurs with a range of psychiatric conditions, creating an important global public health challenge. However, neurobiological research on these associations remains fragmented across disciplines, and a systematic bibliometric synthesis is lacking.

Objective

To map the knowledge structure, identify research hotspots, and characterize temporal trends in neurobiological research linking obesity with selected psychiatric conditions.

Methods

Relevant literature (2010-2025) was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Following screening, 476 studies were included. Bibliometric and visualization analyses were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Scimago Graphica. A supplementary Scopus analysis assessed publication overlap and concordance in selected bibliometric indicators.

Results

Publications surged after 2021, with the last 5 years accounting for 54.2% of the total. The United States and China had the highest publication counts. Among the 10 most productive countries, France had the highest mean annualized citations per publication. Core hotspots include neuroinflammation, the gut-brain axis, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysfunction, and high-fat diet.

Conclusion

Neuroinflammation, the gut-brain axis, and HPA-axis-related processes emerged as recurring themes. These findings highlight the need for further investigation of metabolic, immune, and neural processes in geographically diverse populations, particularly in developing regions.

articles.abstractText: Understanding the spatial dynamics of genetic ancestry is essential for elucidating historical and contemporary patterns of gene flow among populations. Honey bees in the United States have a 400-year history of importation, management, and adaptation to diverse environments. Genetic diversity is a key factor for colony health and resilience. Notably, the most genetically diverse populations in the country originate from the invasive A-lineage (Africanized or 'Killer' honey bees). In this study, we leveraged a nationwide community-science platform to assemble an extensive genomic dataset of U.S. honey bee populations and used it to ask how this invasive lineage is spreading across the country and how its spread has impacted honey bee genetic diversity nationwide. Using RFMix, we assigned local ancestry across the genome to capture fine-scale ancestry patterns and applied TreeMix to genome-wide allele frequency data to infer directional gene flow among U.S. populations. Our analyses revealed patterns consistent with a strong northward migration, with major source populations in southern states such as Texas (TX), Arizona (AZ), and Florida (FL), and primary targets in northern states including Michigan (MI), New York (NY), and Vermont (VT). Covariance estimates indicated strong genetic connectivity, particularly from TX and AZ. Spatial visualization of migration edges highlighted key routes of A-lineage expansion. Together, these results provide the first genome-wide evidence for a nationwide spread of A-lineage ancestry in the U.S., offering insights to guide breeding strategies and predict the future dynamics of honey bee genetic diversity.

articles.abstractText: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under-expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent-vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large-scale OCT adoption, including time-consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT-guided optimization, and recent advances in AI-driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI-driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid-rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug-coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI-enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging-physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI-empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.

articles.abstractText: BACKGROUND. Conventional deep learning reconstruction (DLR) CT methods provide noise reduction but limited improvements in spatial resolution. OBJECTIVE. The purpose of this study was to compare a novel superresolution DLR (SR-DLR) algorithm and a hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) algorithm in terms of stent visualization and diagnostic performance for in-stent restenosis on coronary CTA, with invasive coronary angiography (ICA) used as the reference. METHODS. This prospective study enrolled patients undergoing coronary CTA at 11 centers in China from September 2023 to November 2024. Participants underwent coronary CTA performed using a normal-resolution 320-MDCT scanner with reconstruction of HIR and SR-DLR images. The final study sample included participants with a coronary stent who underwent ICA within 2 months after CTA. The stent CNR (CNRstent), stent-lumen attenuation increase ratio (SAIR), and stent edge sharpness were calculated. Two radiologists (reader 1 [R1], reader 2 [R2]) independently assessed stents for subjective image quality (scale of 1-5, with 5 denoting highest quality), diagnostic confidence (scale of 1-5, with 5 indicating greatest confidence), and in-stent restenosis (defined as ≥ 50% stenosis). HIR and SR-DLR were compared using ICA as the reference standard for in-stent restenosis. RESULTS. The analysis included 73 participants (62 men and 11 women; mean age, 65.5 ± 10.3 [SD] years) with 110 stents. SR-DLR, compared with HIR, showed greater mean CNRstent (44.0 ± 20.1 [SD] vs 33.6 ± 15.7), lower mean SAIR (0.44 ± 0.36 [SD] vs 0.71 ± 0.55), and greater mean edge sharpness (469 ± 261 [SD] vs 221 ± 130 HU/mm) (all p < .05). SR-DLR, compared with HIR, showed greater subjective image quality (both readers: median score, 4 vs 3) and greater diagnostic confidence (both readers: median score, 4 vs 3) (all p < .001). SR-DLR, compared with HR, showed greater accuracy for in-stent restenosis among all stents in per-stent analysis (R1: 89.1% vs 79.1%; R2: 88.2% vs 77.3%) and per-patient analysis (R1: 89.0% vs 79.5%; R2: 87.7% vs 72.6%) and among stents with a diameter of 3.0 mm or less in per-stent analysis (R1: 91.5% vs 81.4%; R2: 93.2% vs 81.4%) and per-patient analysis (R1: 90.7% vs 76.7%; R2: 93.0% vs 76.7%). CONCLUSION. SR-DLR, compared with HIR, yielded objective and subjective improvements in stent visualization, including differences attributable to reduced blooming artifacts, and greater diagnostic performance for in-stent restenosis. CLINICAL IMPACT. The novel SR-DLR algorithm improves the performance of coronary CTA obtained using conventional 320-MDCT scanners and could support the expanded use of CTA for stent evaluation. articles.abstractText: Neonatal sepsis and genetic disorders share overlapping clinical presentations in critically ill neonates, making differential diagnosis challenging. We report an incidental detection of herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) through human genome sequencing (GS) initially performed for suspected genetic disease. A 7-day-old male infant presented with fever and failure to gain weight. Initial investigations revealed inflammatory response and gram-positive cocci in urine; CSF and respiratory microbiological analyses were negative. Trio-based GS was performed under the French Genomic Medicine Plan 2025. Soft-clipped reads from BAM files were analyzed using IGV visualization and NCBI BLAST homology search. Retrospective virological testing was performed on archived samples. GS variant calling initially identified an apparent de novo insertion in NRROS. Manual BAM file inspection revealed that flanking soft-clipped sequences aligned with the HSV-1 UL47 gene rather than the human genome. Retrospective PCR confirmed HSV-1 in blood and nasopharyngeal samples, despite initially negative CSF testing. The patient died at 14 days of age from disseminated HSV-1 infection with multiorgan failure. Human GS can incidentally detect pathogen sequences through systematic analysis of unmapped reads, highlighting its potential dual diagnostic utility in neonatal intensive care.

articles.abstractText:
Objectives

Conventional hemodynamic assessment of Fontan circulation relies on limited quantitative measurements. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical value of comprehensive flow visualization using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging to characterize patient-specific hemodynamic patterns in extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection.

Methods

Eight patients with extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection underwent four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging at a median of 13.7 years postoperatively (interquartile range: 9.0-16.4 years). The Fontan pathway was segmented into five regions: extracardiac conduit, superior vena cava, central confluence, left pulmonary artery, and right pulmonary artery. Energy loss, maximum velocity, and kinetic energy were quantified for each segment using iTFlow software. Clinical outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

Results

Median age at total cavopulmonary connection was 1.8 years (interquartile range: 1.5-3.5), with 18 mm conduits in seven patients and 22 mm conduit in one patient. During a median follow-up of 17.3 years, two patients underwent re-operation after magnetic resonance imaging evaluation (tricuspid valve replacement and ascending aortic reconstruction); all remained alive without Fontan failure. Energy loss differed significantly across segments (p = 0.011), being highest in the conduit and central confluence, with remarkable inter-patient variability superimposed (conduit values varying 35-fold from 0.025 to 0.887 mW). Maximum velocity strongly correlated with energy loss (r = 0.92, p = 0.001), suggesting velocity may serve as an accessible surrogate. Atrioventricular valve regurgitation severity did not consistently correlate with energy loss.

Conclusions

Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging with iTFlow software enables comprehensive hemodynamic assessment throughout the Fontan pathway, revealing substantial patient-specific heterogeneity in energy efficiency. With larger cohorts and correlation with clinical outcomes, this technique may become a valuable screening tool for post-Fontan evaluation and long-term surveillance.

These findings support the technical feasibility, workflow efficiency, and short-term corrective effect of the proposed system. articles.abstractText: Sex is a critical determinant of cancer susceptibility, clinical prognosis, and therapeutic response. Sex chromosome aberrations, particularly somatic loss of the Y chromosome (LOY) in male malignancies, exert profound impacts on transcriptional regulation, tumor immune microenvironment remodeling, and malignant progression, highlighting an urgent demand for comprehensive integration of single-cell and spatial omics profiles dissecting sex-biased and LOY landscapes across human cancers. Here, we developed XYcellAtlas (http://www.xycellatlas.top/), an integrative database for integration and multidimensional visualization of sex disparities and LOY features across human tissues at single-cell transcriptomic, epigenomic, and spatial-transcriptomic resolutions. This resource aggregates data from 6764 patient samples covering 18 cancer types, eight precancerous lesions, and 21 tissue origins, encompassing over 25.8 million single cells and one million spatial-transcriptomic spots. Leveraging random forest classifiers trained on normal tissue datasets, XYcellAtlas quantifies cell-type-specific LOY frequencies across cell types. Furthermore, it systematically catalogs sex-biased and LOY-associated molecular alterations, including differentially expressed genes, chromatin peaks, core transcription factors, as well as their functional annotations and dysregulatory signatures within malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment. In summary, XYcellAtlas provides a unified, all-in-one analytical platform enabling researchers to query, inspect, quantify, and visualize sex-associated and LOY-derived multi-omics features underlying tumor evolutionary processes.

articles.abstractText: Despite the apparent simplicity of the motor action involved during percutaneous needle procedures, manipulating the tool's direction becomes challenging when clinicians cannot directly visualize internal anatomy and must rely on ultrasound images, which increase cognitive demand. Augmented reality (AR) offers the promise to assist with these tasks by providing pertinent visual information in the clinician's field of view. However, simply providing visual information that ignores meaningful visual cues can complicate depth perception and spatial understanding. In this work, we introduce and evaluate three visualization techniques for needle alignment developed during design sessions with medical experts: a localized focus-and-context window, a color-based proximity encoding, and an explicit trajectory overlay. These techniques were evaluated in a user study (n = 26) including clinical experts (n = 7) using a prostate-biopsy-inspired phantom. Results from this study suggest that cue effects depended on the surrounding cue configuration and user expertise. For experts, the focus-and-context window reduced completion time and retreat events, while color-based proximity overlay improved completion time. Subjectively, color cues were often perceived as helpful even when their effects on accuracy were not consistent. These results suggest that AR guidance strategies for percutaneous interventions should consider user expertise and visual context.

articles.abstractText: Digital cytology, telecytology, and artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping cytopathology by expanding access to primary diagnosis, remote rapid on-site evaluation, consultation, quality assurance, education, archiving, and research. This review summarizes the technological basis of digital cytology, its current clinical and educational applications, implementation strategies, telecytology platforms, and emerging AI tools in gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytology. Compared with surgical pathology, digital cytology faces greater technical challenges because cytologic specimens often contain three-dimensional cell clusters, variable thickness, and overlapping cells, which increase demands on focusing, scanning time, image storage, and infrastructure. Recent advances in z-stacking, extended depth of focus, and whole-slide imaging have improved digital visualization, while updated professional guidance has supported broader validation of digital cytology for primary diagnosis and rapid on-site evaluation. Telecytology has shown high diagnostic concordance and has improved access to expert assessment, particularly for rapid on-site evaluation in resource-limited or remote settings. AI applications have shown promising performance in screening, classification, and quality control, especially in cervical cytology, with expanding use in non-gynecologic specimens. However, implementation remains constrained by technical complexity, variable image quality, regulatory and medicolegal concerns, infrastructure requirements, cost, and the need for robust validation and training. Overall, digital cytology and AI are guiding the transition into a Cytopathology 2.0 era characterized by greater connectivity, scalability, and data‑driven practice, although widespread adoption will depend on further standardization, robust validation, and smooth integration into everyday workflows.

articles.abstractText:
Background

The vertebral artery (VA) develops through a complex embryological process, and various anatomic variations may be encountered in adults. Vertebral artery fenestration (VAF) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly that may mimic vertebral artery dissection on imaging and requires careful differentiation based on vascular morphology and imaging findings. The coexistence of vertebral artery origin nonopacification, fenestration, and external carotid artery-derived collateral circulation is uncommon.

Case presentation

A 45-year-old man with no history of cerebrovascular disease or conventional vascular risk factors underwent magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) during a routine health examination. MRA revealed multiple cerebrovascular abnormalities, including bilateral vertebral artery stenosis, terminal basilar artery fenestration, persistent fetal-type right posterior cerebral artery, distal stenosis of the bilateral posterior cerebral arteries, stenosis at the bilateral anterior cerebral artery A1/A2 junctions, and cerebral atherosclerotic changes. The patient was asymptomatic, without neurological manifestations such as headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diplopia, rotational vertigo, choking during drinking, dysphagia, or bowel and bladder dysfunction. Whole-brain digital subtraction angiography (DSA) was subsequently performed to further characterize the vascular anatomy.Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated nonopacification of the origin of the right vertebral artery, suggesting proximal occlusion. Selective right external carotid artery angiography revealed collateral vessels originating from branches of the deep cervical artery, costocervical trunk, and occipital artery. These vessels provided collateral supply to the V3 segment of the right vertebral artery through muscular anastomoses, resulting in reconstitution of the distal vertebral artery and visualization of the posterior circulation.

Conclusion

This case demonstrates a rare pattern of complex vertebral artery anatomic variation. DSA not only identified the location of vertebral artery occlusion but also demonstrated the origin of abnormal collateral circulation and the pattern of vascular reconstruction, providing important diagnostic information for complex vertebral artery variations.

articles.abstractText: This report describes a novel case of exostosis on the medial aspect of the sustentaculum tali, (ST) associated with tibiotarsal joint (TTJ) pathology, without involvement of the tarsal sheath or lateral digital flexor tendon. A 5-year-old Standardbred gelding was presented with right TTJ effusion and exercise-induced hind-limb lameness. Diagnostic imaging identified a columnar periosteal proliferation on the medial ST, accompanied by synovial effusion and joint capsule thickening; however, the tarsal sheath and lateral digital flexor tendon remained unremarkable. Although TTJ arthroscopy confirmed synovitis, it did not allow visualization of the exostosis. The lesion was successfully excised via an ultrasound-guided extra-articular surgical approach. Postoperative management included a structured rehabilitation program, resulting in a return to full-speed training by Day 76 with no recurrence of lameness. Follow-up evaluations demonstrated improved performance and complete resolution of TTJ effusion and associated swelling. This case highlighted the importance of multimodal imaging in identifying extra-synovial lesions of the ST and supported ultrasound-guided extra-articular removal as an effective surgical option for ST exostosis. Although the underlying cause of the lesion was uncertain, subclinical trauma was considered a likely contributing factor. Key clinical message: The ST is a horizontal bony projection on the plantaromedial aspect of the calcaneus. Due to its minimal soft-tissue coverage, it is particularly vulnerable to external trauma and subsequent osseous proliferation. Exostosis of the ST may result in impingement of the plantaromedial pouch of the tarsocrural (tibiotarsal) joint, contributing to joint irritation and secondary pathology. Accurate diagnosis and effective case management rely on the combined use of radiography and ultrasonography, which together enable detailed assessment of both osseous changes and associated soft-tissue structures.

articles.abstractText: The theranostic paradigm, combining molecular diagnosis and targeted radionuclide therapy in a single platform, has revolutionized precision oncology. Radiopharmaceutical theranostics enables targeted visualization, characterization, and treatment of malignancies through tumor-associated molecular targets, including prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA), somatostatin receptors (SSTR), and fibroblast activation protein (FAP). The approvals of <sup>177</sup>Lu-DOTATATE (Lutathera®) for GEP-NETs and <sup>177</sup>Lu-PSMA-617 (Pluvicto®) for mCRPC are groundbreaking advances that have triggered exponential growth in the field: the VISION study showed a 38% reduction in the risk of death with <sup>177</sup>Lu-PSMA-617, and NETTER-1 a 79% reduction in the risk of progression with <sup>177</sup>Lu-DOTATATE in midgut NETs. Beyond beta emitters, targeted alpha therapy (TAT) with actinium-225, radium-223, and lead-212 is emerging as a powerful strategy to overcome beta-particle resistance, as the high linear energy transfer of alpha particles delivers greater cytotoxicity even in radioresistant tumors. Novel targets such as FAP, CXCR4, HER2, and gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) are further diversifying the theranostic armamentarium across malignancies. This review synthesizes the current status of the field, spanning the radiobiology of targeted radionuclide therapy, clinical evidence from pivotal and ongoing trials, alpha-emitting radioisotopes, next-generation radioligands, the growing role of AI-enabled personalized dosimetry, and combination therapies with immunotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors. We also address current challenges heterogeneous target expression, dose-limiting toxicities, radionuclide supply-chain constraints, and the regulatory framework as well as future directions poised to expand the theranostic paradigm to a broader range of cancers.

articles.abstractText: Collagen organization within the tumour microenvironment plays a critical role in tumour progression and has emerged as an important structural biomarker in cancer. Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) microscopy enables label-free visualization and quantitative assessment of fibrillar collagen architecture; however, its high cost, specialized instrumentation, and limited field-of-view restrict routine clinical application. In this study, we evaluated whether collagen features quantified from digitally scanned Masson-Goldner's Trichrome-stained histopathological sections can approximate measurements obtained from SHG microscopy. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded breast tumour tissues, including benign and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) samples with varying collagen content, were analysed using SHG microscopy and whole-slide brightfield imaging. Matched regions of interest were analysed using two independent digital image analysis approaches: a conventional ImageJ-based workflow (TWOMBLI) and a machine learning-based computational pipeline. Collagen structural parameters including collagen deposition area, fibre number, and alignment metrics were quantified and compared across imaging modalities using correlation analysis. SHG signals were consistently detected from Trichrome-stained sections, confirming compatibility of SHG imaging. Quantitative comparison demonstrated significant concordance between SHG-derived collagen metrics and those obtained from digital image analysis pipelines, particularly for collagen area and fibre alignment. These findings demonstrate a proof-of-concept, that computational analysis of routine histopathological images can capture key spatial features of collagen organization comparable to SHG microscopy. Digital pathology-based collagen quantification therefore represents a potentially scalable and clinically accessible approach for assessing extracellular matrix architecture in tumour tissues.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Multifidus muscle tears are uncommon injuries, and herniation of muscle tissue into the spinal canal has not been previously reported. This report presents a rare case of traumatic multifidus muscle herniation into the spinal canal, leading to cauda equina syndrome. The primary research question is whether a specific sequential injury mechanism can explain this unusual pattern of intraspinal muscle herniation.

Methods

An 18-year-old woman presented with back pain, bilateral lower limb and perineal numbness, lower extremity weakness, and urinary retention after a fall from height. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an intraspinal soft tissue mass at the L2 level causing thecal sac compression, consistent with cauda equina syndrome. The patient underwent urgent decompressive laminectomy with pedicle screw fixation from T12 to L3 and underwent posterolateral bone graft fusion at L1 to L2. Intraoperative findings and histopathological examination confirmed the nature of the compressive mass.

Results

Preoperative imaging, intraoperative visualization, and postoperative pathology confirmed that the intraspinal mass represented herniated multifidus muscle tissue. At 6-month follow-up, the patient demonstrated complete neurological recovery without residual symptoms. The proposed mechanism involves sequential hyperflexion and hyperextension forces during the traumatic event, potentially creating a transient osseous gap allowing muscle herniation.

Conclusions

This rare case demonstrates that traumatic hyperflexion-hyperextension injury can result in intraspinal herniation of the multifidus muscle, leading to cauda equina syndrome. Recognition of this potential mechanism may aid in diagnosis and timely surgical intervention.

Clinical relevance

Clinicians should consider soft tissue herniation, including muscle, in the differential diagnosis of traumatic intraspinal masses causing neurological compromise. Prompt surgical decompression can achieve excellent neurological outcomes.

articles.abstractText: Rectal cancer patients show significant heterogeneity in their response to neoadjuvant therapy, which stems from the differential remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment caused by chemoradiotherapy. Currently, there is a lack of monitoring methods to capture this immune activation signal early in clinical practice. To address this, we developed liquid-gas phase change lipid nanoparticles targeting CXCL10 for non-invasive ultrasound molecular imaging to monitor tumor immune responses during neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. We analyzed the expression of CXCL10 in colorectal cancer tissues and its correlation with patient prognosis, as well as CXCL10's ability of chemotactism to T cells. We constructed phase-change lipid nanoparticles modified with CXCL10 antibodies (aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid), and systematically assessed in vitro physicochemical properties, antibody modification, cell uptake, and phase transformation efficiency. In mouse rectal cancer models, we evaluated biosafety, biodistribution, ultrasound imaging, and chemoradiotherapy efficacy, followed by testing the immune microenvironment of tumor tissues. CXCL10 was highly expressed in macrophages and a distinct subset of tumor‑enriched endothelial cells, and the abundance of this endothelial subset correlated significantly with favorable prognosis. The CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling axis was a key pathway mediating the chemotactic migration of CD8⁺ T cells. The aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid nanoparticles exhibited uniform size (62.97 ± 0.83 nm) and excellent tumor targeting. Upon low-intensity pulsed ultrasound irradiation, nanoparticles underwent phase transition to microbubbles, producing markedly increased contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) signals. After chemoradiotherapy, the treatment group showed an increase in CXCL10 expression levels, as well as the CEUS signals. Compared to the untreated control group, the tumor suppression rate reached 89.45%, with an increasing expression of CD4⁺, CD8⁺, CD3+ and CD68⁺ in tumor tissue, while decreased Foxp3. The aCXCL10/PFP@Lipid enables effective ultrasound molecular visualization of CXCL10 expression, offering a potential novel noninvasive strategy for monitoring of the tumor immune microenvironment and treatment response in colorectal cancer.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.

Objective

The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a transformer-based model for generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis by modeling long-range temporal dependencies and complex relationships in heterogeneous EHR data and to examine its interpretability.

Methods

We developed the Biomarker-Aware Transformer for AKI (BAT-AKI), which integrates multidimensional embeddings capturing temporal dynamics, textual descriptions, hierarchical ontology structures, and semantic relationships in EHRs. To enhance sensitivity to AKI-related biomarker fluctuations, BAT-AKI combines masked language modeling with a novel biomarker abnormality-aware pretraining task. The model was pretrained and fine-tuned for 4 tasks: AKI onset, early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality. Pretraining and internal validation used data from the National Patient-Centered Clinical Research Network (PCORnet) site, with external validation across 3 additional sites.

Results

BAT-AKI achieved the strongest overall discrimination, outperforming baseline models in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) on most tasks. For AKI onset prediction, it achieved an AUROC of 0.8549 (95% CI 0.8433-0.8658) and an AUPRC of 0.6041 (95% CI 0.5786-0.6292), exceeding the second-best baseline by 2.8% in AUROC and 8.1% in AUPRC. Across prognostic tasks, BAT-AKI achieved AUROCs of 0.6006 (95% CI 0.5703-0.6318), 0.6080 (95% CI 0.5745-0.6397), and 0.8017 (95% CI 0.7708-0.8311) and AUPRCs of 0.7036 (95% CI 0.6690-0.7388), 0.7417 (95% CI 0.7082-0.7765), and 0.5063 (95% CI 0.4422-0.5684) for early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality, respectively, corresponding to relative gains of 2.4% to 6% in AUROC and 3.7% to 4.1% in AUPRC over the second-best baseline. Performance remained stable across external cohorts, with AKI onset AUROCs ranging from 0.7754 (95% CI 0.7677-0.7827) to 0.7989 (95% CI 0.7885-0.8092) and AUPRCs ranging from 0.4777 (95% CI 0.4631-0.4924) to 0.5687 (95% CI 0.5495-0.5871), corresponding to relative improvements of 3.7% to 5.3% in AUROC and 16.8% to 25.3% in AUPRC over the transformer baseline. In a low-resource setting using only 2% of the fine-tuning data, BAT-AKI achieved an AUROC of 0.7898 (95% CI 0.7759-0.8036) and an AUPRC of 0.4903 (95% CI 0.4640-0.5178) for AKI onset prediction, exceeding the second-best baseline by 4.2% in AUROC and 10.9% in AUPRC. Visualization of embeddings, attention patterns, and integrated-gradient feature attributions highlighted clinically meaningful relationships and patient-specific trajectories.

Conclusions

BAT-AKI provides generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis with consistent discrimination across institutions, while offering interpretability insights into its predictions, supporting its potential for early warning and AKI care optimization.

Rationale and objectives

To develop and validate an ultrasound-based habitat radiomics framework for the hierarchical differentiation of tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) from non-tuberculous lymphadenopathy, and to noninvasively predict rifampicin resistance risk using an independently collected cohort of patients with confirmed TBLN.

Materials and methods

In this multicenter retrospective study, 618 patients with superficial lymphadenopathy who underwent ultrasound examination between January 2022 and December 2025 at four tertiary hospitals were included. Among them, 530 patients with definitive diagnoses were used for diagnostic differentiation and were divided into a model-development (training) cohort and an external validation cohort, while 236 patients with confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) were included for rifampicin resistance risk assessment. Based on standardized B-mode ultrasound images, we developed a 2-stage ultrasound habitat radiomics framework that first differentiated tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes. Rifampicin resistance risk was assessed within the confirmed TBLN cohort using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA), and model interpretability was assessed using SHAP-based methods.

Results

For differentiating tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes, the habitat-based model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 in the training cohort and maintaining consistent performance in the external test cohort. Using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions within the confirmed TBLN cohort, the habitat-based model achieved an AUC of 0.83 for predicting rifampicin resistance, outperforming conventional radiomics and demonstrating superior clinical net benefit. Spatial visualization revealed that high-risk habitats were localized to specific intralesional regions, underscoring the importance of spatial heterogeneity in both disease diagnosis and drug resistance assessment.

Conclusion

Ultrasound-based habitat radiomics provides an interpretable and clinically applicable framework for hierarchical diagnosis of tuberculous lymphadenitis and for rifampicin resistance risk assessment in an independent patient cohort, supporting precision imaging-guided management of tuberculosis.

articles.abstractText:
Purpose

To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of a minimal-volume, single-mesh technique for dual-cervicovaginal wall fixation in abdominal sacrohysteropexy.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, 38 patients who underwent abdominal sacrohysteropexy using a single specially designed mesh fixed to both the anterior and posterior cervico-vaginal walls and anchored to the sacral promontory were included and evaluated. Objective and subjective outcomes, as well as complications, were evaluated over a median follow-up of 17 months (range, 12-60).

Results

The median age was 65 years (interquartile range, 58-72). Due to combined anterior-compartment defects and/or urodynamic stress urinary incontinence, bilateral paravaginal defect repair and anti-incontinence surgery (Burch colposuspension) were performed in 76.3% and 52.6% of patients, respectively. Among the 38 patients who completed at least 1 year of follow-up, no objective recurrence of apical prolapse and no other vaginal prolapse greater than Stage 1 were observed. Statistically significant improvements were found after surgery in some prolapse-related symptoms, such as bulge sensation or visualization, pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, sensation of incomplete bladder emptying, and urinary incontinence. All patients reported subjective improvement, with 30/38 (78.9%) reporting being "very much better," 7/38 (18.4%) "much better," and 1/38 (2.6%) "a little better". Postoperative complications were mostly minor. De novo stress urinary incontinence developed in two patients (5.2%); one was managed conservatively (2.6%) (Grade I), while the other required stress urinary incontinence surgery (2.6%) (Grade III). No cases of mesh erosion, mesh exposure, spondylodiscitis, sacral osteomyelitis, or middle sacral vein injury were observed during the perioperative or follow-up period.

Conclusions

Dual-cervicovaginal wall fixation using a single minimal-volume mesh appears to be a safe and effective approach for abdominal sacrohysteropexy. This technique may reduce mesh burden without compromising clinical outcomes. Long-term follow-up findings and comparative studies with other techniques are needed.
